frustration.name: Frustration
frustration.description: When things don't go as expected

reasons.frustration: Frustration needs deep emotional processing: 90 seconds help you lower the activation and regain perspective.
reasons.fear: Fear requires immediate clarity. A quick reset redirects your attention without amplifying emotion.
reasons.overthinking: A quick reset breaks the mental loop: it interrupts the paralyzing analysis and gets you back into action.
reasons.overwhelm: Feeling overwhelmed needs immediate focus on the present. The quick mode recalibrates your scattered attention.
reasons.unmotivated: Low motivation is an energy problem. 90 seconds help you reconnect with purpose and meaning.
reasons.tilt: Tilt is extreme emotional activation. It takes time for your nervous system to fully calm down.

calmAnchor.subtitle: This space is for you to set a moment to come back to.
calmAnchor.infoAria: How to use the calm anchor

steps.title: Breathe deeply
steps.body: The main goal is to create separation between you and the emotion. This stops the "psychic entropy."

steps.title: Set the anchor
steps.body: As you say the phrase you're going to anchor, make a small physical gesture (like pressing your thumb). According to Robert Dilts, this is an "anchor": a specific stimulus that automatically evokes a previously associated inner state of calm. The phrase could remind you of a place, a person, a scent…

steps.title: Inject logic
steps.body: Use the phrase to reactivate your rational mind. When emotion runs high, the brain blocks higher functions; breathing and verbalizing lets you "inject logic" and regain your attention.

steps.title: Focus on the present
steps.body: Direct your psychic energy toward a small, immediate goal. Wellbeing appears when there's "order in consciousness," achieved by focusing attention on the here and now.

fastMode.title: Focus & Stability
fastMode.subtitle: Ideal before starting your day or during focus breaks. Keeps your mind clear, cool, and alert.

deepMode.title: Emergency Reset
deepMode.subtitle: Recommended in moments of high pressure, stress, or frustration. Turns off your brain's alarm and helps you regain control right away.

flowState.title: Flow state
flowState.criterion: Keep an activity where the challenge matches your skill for at least 20 minutes.
flowState.reference: The balance between challenge and skill creates total absorption.

firstAlly.title: First ally
firstAlly.criterion: Invite an accountability partner to track a habit together.
firstAlly.reference: Social commitment increases the odds of success.

fiveDayStreak.title: 5-day streak
fiveDayStreak.criterion: Log your habits for 5 days without missing twice in a row.
fiveDayStreak.reference: The "never miss twice" mantra protects consistency.

unstoppable.title: Nothing stops me
unstoppable.criterion: Successfully complete a hard task in an initially unfavorable environment.
unstoppable.reference: Reflects the "autotelic personality" that finds flow in difficulty.

twoMinuteRule.title: Two-minute rule
twoMinuteRule.criterion: Complete the simplified version of a new habit to beat initial resistance.
twoMinuteRule.reference: Standardizing the start matters more than optimizing the outcome.

caterpillarEffect.title: Caterpillar effect
caterpillarEffect.criterion: Identify and fix your most frequent mistake (raise your "worst level").
caterpillarEffect.reference: Real progress happens when you raise your performance floor.

onePercentBetter.title: 1% better daily
onePercentBetter.criterion: Log a small improvement or marginal gain in a specific skill.
onePercentBetter.reference: The accumulation of small gains creates huge changes over time.

closingRitual.title: Closing ritual
closingRitual.criterion: Run your work shutdown steps and say, even just to yourself, "day is closed."
closingRitual.reference: Frees the mind from the Zeigarnik effect (unfinished tasks) so you can rest.

calmAnchor.title: Calm anchor
calmAnchor.criterion: Use a conditioned physical gesture to calm yourself in a tense moment.
calmAnchor.reference: Anchoring lets you recall positive internal states at will.

reframe.name: Perspective and Focus
reframe.tagline: Your focus decides what you see.

cards.title: Are you relying on objective data, or on what you're feeling right now?
cards.message: Treating your personal perceptions as absolute truths tends to make you ignore the objective data you need to decide well.
cards.action: What do you know for certain right now? Name three facts that would still be true even if you felt different today.

cards.title: Does what you're doing right now bring you closer to the person you want to be, or further away?
cards.message: Everything you do, big or small, is a vote that builds the image of who you are and how you act.
cards.action: Describe objectively what you're doing and why, as if you were telling someone else. Then answer: does this bring you closer to or further from the person you want to be? If it moves you further away, adjust one detail now.

cards.title: Is there any hesitation running through your head right now, even a small one?
cards.message: If there is, it's often a way to avoid a risk you haven't processed yet; if there isn't, it's a good moment to confirm you're not avoiding anything.
cards.action: If you spot a doubt, name the risk your fear is trying to avoid; if there's none, check whether there's something you've been putting off.

cards.title: How does your perspective change if you think of this moment as part of something longer, rather than an isolated event?
cards.message: Mastery requires understanding that this moment is just one part of a much bigger series of events.
cards.action: Think of what you're doing right now as a step within something longer (a goal, a routine, a project), and act based on that, not just the instant.

cards.title: What difficulty is likely to show up today, and how do you want to respond when it does?
cards.message: Preparing the "even though" phrase ahead of time keeps it ready for when the pressure hits.
cards.action: Pick a likely situation from today and complete: "Even though [anxiety/pressure] shows up, I'm going to keep going with [your next step]." For example: "Even though anxiety shows up, I'm going to take the next step."

cards.title: Do you feel like something is a threat right now, or are you calm?
cards.message: Changing how you picture a problem helps lower the intensity of the fear; if there's no active threat, this is a good time to practice the technique cold.
cards.action: If there's a threat, picture it smaller, farther away, or less intense — whatever feels most natural to you; if there isn't, practice the same exercise with any uncomfortable memory.

cards.title: How are you breathing right now?
cards.message: The rhythm of your breathing affects your mental clarity, whether or not the situation is under control.
cards.action: Adjust your posture, drop your shoulders, and steady your breathing before continuing with what you're doing.

cards.title: What can you learn from what's happening right now, whether you decide something or not?
cards.message: Every situation can give you useful information if you pay attention, even when it doesn't look like it at first glance.
cards.action: Name something you just noticed right now (in your surroundings, your body, or your task) and think about how you could use it.

cards.title: What matters most to you to protect today, even if it means not being right?
cards.message: Pride tends to win out over what truly matters to you without you noticing; identifying it ahead of time gives you the edge to stop it in time.
cards.action: The next time today you feel the urge to push your point of view, choose to yield instead of insisting — even if you're right.

cards.title: What evidence do you have that you've already solved situations like this before?
cards.message: Confidence based on concrete experience is more solid than a repeated affirmation; looking back gives you real data, not just intention.
cards.action: Name one specific past situation you already solved that's similar to what you're facing today.

regulation.name: Balance and Presence
regulation.tagline: The body decides before the mind does.

cards.title: If your body is on alert right now, is it real danger or just an emotional reaction?
cards.message: Very high stress can make it hard to think clearly, pushing you to decide on pure impulse.
cards.action: Put your hand on your stomach and make sure it's moving with your breath; if it's not moving, you're probably in stress mode.

cards.title: What signals from your body do you tend to mistake for current alarms, when they're actually echoes of the past?
cards.message: Recognizing the pattern ahead of time helps you spot it faster when it shows up.
cards.action: Recall the last time you mixed up a signal like that, and mentally note how it felt so you can recognize it today if it comes back.

cards.title: What's the main goal you want to accomplish this exact instant?
cards.message: Defining a single purpose right now keeps random thoughts from throwing you off course and creating chaos.
cards.action: Define in one sentence what your immediate goal is.

cards.title: Can you put an exact name to the emotion running through your body?
cards.message: Putting words to what you feel helps you stop reacting on impulse and start thinking more clearly.
cards.action: Name the emotion as precisely as you can (not just "bad," but exactly what kind) and notice how its intensity shifts as you do.

cards.title: If you had a physical switch for calm, where would you put it on your body?
cards.message: If you already have a calming gesture, use it; if not, pick a simple pressure point to bring back your focus right now.
cards.action: Pick a simple physical gesture (e.g. pressing your thumb against your index finger) that from today on you'll associate with returning to the present, and use it now.

cards.title: Does your emotional state let you think clearly?
cards.message: There's a level of agitation beyond which the mind stops evaluating reality and just reacts automatically.
cards.action: If you have something to decide, wait a mandatory 10 seconds; if not, take a 10-second pause before continuing what you're doing.

cards.title: If you need a push right now, what past achievement would give it to you?
cards.message: Bringing a past win to mind can help you restore the confidence and focus you need right now.
cards.action: Recall a moment when you solved a difficult situation and notice how you acted, before getting back to what you're doing.

cards.title: If you hear a critical voice right now, is it a reproach, or a real signal from your body?
cards.message: That inner voice that criticizes you tends to use guilt to control you; a genuine bodily signal feels different — more like information than an attack.
cards.action: Notice if the voice in your head sounds like a reproach; if it does, ignore it and return to your body's sensations.

cards.title: If you're in the middle of something right now, are you reacting on impulse, or responding from awareness?
cards.message: Between what happens and what you do, there's a gap where you can choose not to act automatically.
cards.action: Take a pause of two full breathing cycles to widen your capacity for observation before you act.

cards.title: Can you feel your weight and your feet on the ground?
cards.message: Losing touch with your body under stress lowers your precision; feeling present again brings back immediate control.
cards.action: Press your feet firmly into the ground for 3 seconds to "ground" your senses in the present.

flow.name: Action and Focus
flow.tagline: All your power fits into the next second.

cards.title: Are you still thinking about something that's already over?
cards.message: Continuing to think about earlier tasks or events drains the mental energy you need for what you're doing now.
cards.action: Consciously decide that what happened is over, and bring your attention back to the present.

cards.title: What's the one concrete action that demands your attention this second?
cards.message: The real cost of a distraction isn't always the distraction itself, but the time it takes you to refocus.
cards.action: Say "now" and get back to the task right away. Before you do, check that it's really the task that deserves your attention right now.

cards.title: If someone were watching you right now, would they say you're focused on what you're doing?
cards.message: Forgetting about yourself is key to performing well; the ego burns energy you need to decide.
cards.action: Bring your full attention to the task, not to how you're being seen.

cards.title: Is this the most important thing you could be doing right now?
cards.message: Naming your immediate intention helps you focus your attention and act with precision.
cards.action: Define the goal of your next minute in under three words. If you realize it's not the highest-impact task, redirect your attention before you start.

cards.title: Are you processing what's happening now, or simulating a future that doesn't exist yet?
cards.message: Focusing on what's happening right now stops the anxiety of imagining future problems or outcomes.
cards.action: Name three things happening right in front of you right now (sounds, movements, people), without judging them. Then deliberately return to what you were doing before this pause.

cards.title: Is there something more important that your attention is leaving out right now?
cards.message: Paying attention to subtle changes lets you adjust your behavior before something becomes a problem.
cards.action: If something comes to mind (a task or a sign you're overlooking), name it, and if it changes your priorities, readjust your focus; if nothing comes to mind, that's a good sign you're already well focused.

cards.title: If some trivial distraction is stealing your focus right now, what is it?
cards.message: Deep work demands sustained concentration; irrelevant distractions can lower the quality of what you do.
cards.action: Physically move any object or notification that isn't essential to what you're doing out of your sight.

cards.title: What's the smallest detail you can pick up on right now?
cards.message: Relevant details often set apart good execution; flow shows up when you notice what others miss.
cards.action: Focus your gaze on a single texture or specific number and hold it for 3 seconds before acting. If that detail doesn't change your next action, it's probably noise. Let it go and move on.

cards.title: Is your inner dialogue giving you useful instructions, or is it just noise?
cards.message: A quiet mind lets the security and clarity you need to act with precision come through.
cards.action: For ten seconds, watch your thoughts without following any of them, then bring your attention back to your breathing.

cards.title: Are you immersed in the situation, or watching it as a spectator?
cards.message: Feeling part of the action and sensing control removes the unnecessary fear of risk.
cards.action: Fully commit for the next ten seconds, and when you're done, assess whether this is still the best investment of your attention.

systems.name: Systems and Consistency
systems.tagline: The system wins, not today's result.

cards.title: Is what you're doing right now following a method, or just an impulse of the moment?
cards.message: If you already have a routine or way of doing things, stick to it; if you're acting on the fly, this is a good moment to notice it.
cards.action: Identify whether you're following a method, or just reacting without realizing it, and adjust if needed.

cards.title: Is what you're doing right now actually helping what you want to achieve today?
cards.message: Real progress is built through the accumulation of correct actions, whether they show right away or not.
cards.action: Name your overall goal for today in one sentence, and decide whether what you're doing right now brings you closer to it or further away.

cards.title: What's the simplest, most effective tool you can use right now?
cards.message: Doing the basics well is usually worth more than risking a complicated maneuver to fix a previous mistake.
cards.action: Run the most solid, basic move you know before attempting anything riskier. If you've already tried it several times with no result, it's time to change strategy.

cards.title: Does your environment make it easy to do things right, or does it tempt you into error?
cards.message: Setting up your workspace to avoid distractions tends to work better than trying to resist them with willpower alone.
cards.action: Physically remove the object that tends to tempt you into error from your immediate view.

cards.title: How can you adjust what you're doing right now to make it a bit better?
cards.message: The ability to correct on the fly, even in simple tasks, is a muscle you train every day.
cards.action: Identify one detail in what you're doing right now that you could improve, and apply it now.

cards.title: Do you trust what you know how to do, or does overthinking hold you back?
cards.message: In situations you already know well, acting fluidly tends to be more precise than overanalyzing every step.
cards.action: If you already master what you're doing, count "3, 2, 1" and flow; if it's something new, identify the first technical step and execute it.

cards.title: What part of your day do you already expect will be the hardest?
cards.message: Naming it now, with a cool head, lets you simplify it before the pressure complicates it.
cards.action: Identify that task and define right now what the simplest first step would be to tackle it.

cards.title: Are you already in the hardest moment of your day, or is it still ahead of you?
cards.message: Having your first move decided ahead of time gives you a starting point; if the moment has already arrived, executing it without hesitation is what makes the difference.
cards.action: If you're already in that moment, execute the first step you defined now (or the simplest one you can think of); if it hasn't arrived yet, leave it decided for when it does.

cards.title: If you're about to act fast right now, is it out of rush, or because the situation truly calls for it?
cards.message: Patience tends to be more effective than urgency, even when everything pushes you to resolve things quickly.
cards.action: Before confirming your next action, double-check that it meets your criteria.

cards.title: Does your confidence depend on chance, or on following clear steps?
cards.message: Stable confidence comes from respecting a process, regardless of what happens around you.
cards.action: Tell yourself: "My job is to follow the process; the outcome is just a data point to learn from."

cards.title: What facts are you going to base today's important decisions on?
cards.message: Practicing the logic before you need it makes you faster when the moment arrives.
cards.action: Pick a decision you know you'll have to make today and sum up in one sentence the logic you're going to use.

cards.title: What two factors will define the most important outcome of your day?
cards.message: Identifying them ahead of time lets you ignore the noise as soon as it shows up.
cards.action: Name those two factors now and keep them as your filter for the rest of the day. If at some point you realize you're acting outside that filter, pause for a moment and correct course.

cards.title: If you notice your pride is getting in the way, what might it be making you ignore?
cards.message: Deceiving yourself is a way of protecting the ego; it's worth checking your own biases all the time.
cards.action: Imagine you're your own opponent; what weak point would you find in what you're about to do?

cards.title: If you have something to decide, are you moving on hope or on real information?
cards.message: Certainty is better built by relying on your skills and objective information than by trusting luck.
cards.action: Look for concrete evidence that supports your choice; if you don't have anything to decide right now, check a concrete fact about your surroundings before moving on.

cards.title: What are you going to form a judgment about today, and with what real evidence?
cards.message: Preparing to rely on facts instead of assumptions protects you from jumping to conclusions.
cards.action: Think of a situation you're going to decide on today and mentally note the concrete facts that support it — not what you assume about it.

cards.title: What alternatives do you have available today, whether you're using them or not?
cards.message: Knowing other options exist gives you confidence even when you don't need them yet.
cards.action: Name one alternative or exit route you have available today, even if you don't plan to use it.

cards.title: If you have to decide something right now, what principle do you want to honor?
cards.message: Choosing the principle before acting gives you a clear criterion to decide with, instead of just reacting to the impulse of the moment.
cards.action: Think of one concrete action that's consistent with that principle, and do it now.

cards.title: If something feels overwhelming right now, what would be the first step to shrink it down?
cards.message: Breaking a hard situation into smaller parts lets you solve them one at a time with precision.
cards.action: Identify and solve only the very first step of the sequence in front of you. Before moving on, confirm that step solves the right problem, not just the most comfortable one.

cards.title: Are you aware that the only thing you truly control today is how you act?
cards.message: The final outcome can depend on external factors, but the quality of what you do is what defines your trajectory.
cards.action: Pick one action from your day and do it with determination, accepting that much of what happens afterward is out of your hands.

cards.title: Are you giving your full attention to what actually matters right now?
cards.message: Focusing fully on what matters is what helps you perform best, even though it's hard to sustain all the time.
cards.action: Eliminate every possible interruption for the next 10 minutes.
